title: WTT Finals Hong Kong: Togami, Jorgic, Dang Qiu and Lin Shidong complete the men's field
seo_title: WTT Finals Hong Kong 2026: men's and women's fields
description: WTT has confirmed all 32 singles players for the WTT Finals Hong Kong, 9 to 13 December, with Sora Matsushima top of the men's race ahead of Félix Lebrun.
standfirst: Togami, Jorgic, Dang Qiu and Lin Shidong took the last men's places, Joo Cheonhui and Sabine Winter the last two in the women's field, with Sun Yingsha and Wang Chuqin in mixed doubles.
body: WTT has confirmed the 32 singles players for the WTT Finals Hong Kong, the season-ending event at Kai Tak Arena from 9 to 13 December. Shunsuke Togami, Darko Jorgic, Dang Qiu and Lin Shidong took the last four men's places, while Joo Cheonhui and Sabine Winter filled the final two in the women's field once WTT Star Contender Muscat closed the qualifying window.

The Finals is open to the top 16 singles players in WTT's season race, which counts ITTF World Ranking points earned across 2026, and the top seven doubles teams at the entry deadline. One mixed doubles pair, Sun Yingsha and Wang Chuqin, completes the field through the [wild card announced earlier this month](/news/wtt-finals-hong-kong-2026-mixed-wild-card-wang-chuqin-sun-yingsha.html).

Sora Matsushima finishes the race on top with 7,220 points, 985 clear of Félix Lebrun on 6,235 and 1,200 ahead of Tomokazu Harimoto on 6,020. Harimoto is the defending champion after beating Truls Moregard 4-2 in last year's final. Japan, China and France have the largest groups: three Japanese, four Chinese and both Lebrun brothers, with two Germans, Patrick Franziska and Dang Qiu, and one player each from Brazil, Chinese Taipei, Sweden, South Korea and Slovenia.

The four places still open before Muscat went to Togami, who then won the Star Contender title (see Eleven's [Muscat finals report](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-finals-honoka-hashimoto-shunsuke-togami-titles.html)), Jorgic, Dang Qiu and Lin Shidong. WTT's announcement describes Jorgic, the world No 15, as the first Slovenian to reach a Grand Smash semi-final, at Europe Smash Sweden 2026, and Lin as a former world No 1. Lin, a semi-finalist in Hong Kong a year ago, took the 16th and last place on 2,360 points, 25 clear of Anders Lind and Vladimir Sidorenko, who both finished on 2,335. Hiroto Shinozuka (2,325) and Oh Junsung (2,314) were next.
The men's field in race order, with points:

- Sora Matsushima (JPN) 7,220
- Félix Lebrun (FRA) 6,235
- Tomokazu Harimoto (JPN) 6,020
- Hugo Calderano (BRA) 5,135
- Lin Yun-Ju (TPE) 4,840
- Truls Moregard (SWE) 4,290
- Jang Woojin (KOR) 4,030
- Zhou Qihao (CHN) 3,305
- Patrick Franziska (GER) 3,225
- Shunsuke Togami (JPN) 3,185
- Alexis Lebrun (FRA) 3,130
- Wen Ruibo (CHN) 2,995
- Wang Chuqin (CHN) 2,820
- Dang Qiu (GER) 2,640
- Darko Jorgic (SLO) 2,534
- Lin Shidong (CHN) 2,360

Wang Manyu defends the title she won in 2025 with a 4-2 final win over Kuai Man, who is in the field again. China have seven of the 16 places (Wang Manyu, Kuai Man, Wang Yidi, Sun Yingsha, Chen Xingtong, Chen Yi and Shi Xunyao), joined by Zhu Yuling of Macao. Japan have five: Miwa Harimoto, Satsuki Odo, Hina Hayata, Hitomi Sato and Honoka Hashimoto, who won in Muscat. South Korea's Shin Yubin and Joo Cheonhui and Germany's Sabine Winter complete the field.

Only two places were left after 11 months of the WTT Series. Joo, the third seed in Muscat, beat Wang Xiaotong 3-2 in the last 16 before losing 3-1 to the fifth seed, Bernadette Szőcs, in the quarter-finals, a run that took her to 15th place. WTT says Winter, who is 34, takes the last place after semi-final runs at Singapore Smash and WTT Champions Frankfurt this year.
The women's field, as WTT lists it:

- Miwa Harimoto (JPN)
- Wang Manyu (CHN)
- Kuai Man (CHN)
- Satsuki Odo (JPN)
- Hina Hayata (JPN)
- Wang Yidi (CHN)
- Sun Yingsha (CHN)
- Hitomi Sato (JPN)
- Chen Xingtong (CHN)
- Chen Yi (CHN)
- Zhu Yuling (MAC)
- Honoka Hashimoto (JPN)
- Shin Yubin (KOR)
- Shi Xunyao (CHN)
- Joo Cheonhui (KOR)
- Sabine Winter (GER)

The Finals follow the Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu, which starts on 29 November. Moregard, sixth in the men's race, was left out of Sweden's squad there to concentrate on Hong Kong ([Sweden's squad](/news/mixed-team-world-cup-2026-sweden-squad-moregard-wtt-finals.html)), and the Lebrun brothers are both in the Hong Kong field. WTT has yet to publish the draw order, and Eleven will add it to the [event page](/events/wtt-finals-hong-kong-2026.html) when it does. Results and live scores will run there during the event, with WTT's YouTube broadcast.
